sentences.text: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
This section defines how offshore environmental observations and protected operational networks support safe farm operations.
The Metocean Buoy is designated Copper Finch for operational reference.
The Metocean Buoy measures wind speed and direction, wave height and period, current, air temperature, and barometric pressure.
Sensors are selected and mounted to limit exposure to spray, icing, vibration, and corrosion.
An onboard logger timestamps observations and retains a local history during intermittent communications.
The Vessel AIS Receiver produces a Position Quality Flag when position integrity checks fail or confidence falls below its configured threshold.
The Weather Service uses validated environmental observations in forecast products for offshore planning.
The Weather Analyst reviews forecast limitations and identifies conditions that may affect vessel access or turbine work.
Measurement intervals and alarm thresholds are configured to support both trend analysis and timely operational decisions.
Time synchronization and sensor health are checked as part of routine monitoring.
The Cybersecurity Gateway is designated Quiet Harbor for operational reference.
The Cybersecurity Gateway establishes a controlled boundary between authorized shore-side services and offshore operational networks.
The boundary permits only approved protocols, destinations, and service accounts.
External connectivity is denied by default and enabled only for documented operational needs.
The SCADA Gateway remains responsible for supervisory communications within its defined control scope.
Administrative access requires authenticated individual accounts and role-based authorization.
Privileged sessions are time limited, logged, and reviewed against approved maintenance activity.
The Cybersecurity Analyst monitors gateway events for unusual access patterns and configuration changes.
Loss of the security boundary places remote administrative functions in a restricted state without bypassing local protective controls.
Security events are retained in protected logs for investigation and audit.
Network segmentation limits the effect of a compromised endpoint and supports controlled restoration of service.
Interfaces are tested after configuration changes to confirm that permitted functions remain available and prohibited paths remain blocked.
Operational procedures identify the authority for approving access, responding to alarms, and returning affected services to normal operation.
